title: “Plip!” by Rita Pavone
text: Rita Ori Filomena Merk-Pavone is an Italian-Swiss pop singer, actress and showgirl, who rose to prominence in the 1960s. Known as "the Mosquito of Turin" (la Zanzara di Torino), she was also nicknamed "Carrot Hair" (Pel di carota) because of the red color of her hair.

title: “La festa” by Adriano Celentano
text: Adriano Celentano is an Italian singer-songwriter, actor, showman, and filmmaker. He is dubbed Il Molleggiato ('the springy one') because of his energetic dancing.

title: “Lei” by Adamo
text: "Elle..." is a French language song, written and sung by Belgian-Italian singer Salvatore Adamo. It was released in late 1964.

title: “Dio, come ti amo” by Domenico Modugno
text: "Dio, come ti amo" is a song recorded by both Italian singers Domenico Modugno and Gigliola Cinquetti, composed and written by Modugno himself. The song won the Sanremo Music Festival 1966 and represented Italy – performed by Modugno – in the Eurovision Song Contest 1966, held in Luxembourg.
listen: Dio, come ti amo Domenico Modugno

title: “Nessuno mi può giudicare” by Caterina Caselli
text: "Nessuno mi può giudicare" is an Italian pop song written by Luciano Beretta, Miki Del Prete, Daniele Pace and Mario Panzeri. The song premiered at the sixteenth edition of the Sanremo Music Festival, and was performed by Caterina Caselli and Gene Pitney, finishing second.
listen: Nessuno mi può giudicare Caterina Caselli

title: “Michelle” by The Beatles
text: "Michelle" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles from their 1965 album Rubber Soul. It was composed principally by Paul McCartney, with the middle eight co-written with John Lennon.

title: “Tema” by I Giganti
text: I Giganti are an Italian pop band founded in 1964. In the 1960s, they had a number of hits including Una ragazza in due, an Italian version of Mister Murray's Down Comes the Rain.

title: “Che colpa abbiamo noi” by The Rokes
text: The Rokes were a pop rock band formed in 1963 in Italy by English expatriates. Their most successful songs included "Piangi con me", the original version of "Let's Live for Today", a US hit when covered by The Grass Roots; and "Che colpa abbiamo noi", an Italian-language version of "Cheryl's Going Home" by Bob Lind.
listen: Che colpa abbiamo noi The Rokes

title: “Notte di ferragosto” by Gianni Morandi
text: Gian Luigi "Gianni" Morandi is an Italian pop singer, actor and entertainer. It is estimated that Morandi has sold about 50 million recordings.

title: “Strangers in the Night” by Frank Sinatra
text: "Strangers in the Night" is a song composed by Bert Kaempfert with English lyrics by Charles Singleton and Eddie Snyder. Kaempfert originally used it under the title "Beddy Bye" as part of the instrumental score for the movie A Man Could Get Killed.
listen: Strangers in the Night Frank Sinatra

title: “Bang Bang” by Equipe 84
text: "Bang Bang" is the second single by American singer-actress Cher from her second album, The Sonny Side of Chér (1966). It was written by her husband Sonny Bono and released in 1966.
